depth_justification: The same block of five reflection questions (anonymization, DPAs, transparency, security, accountability) is repeated verbatim across six consecutive turns (Questions 8 through 37 are recycled) with zero progression, and the genuinely ZenSpace-specific issue (selling employee mood data to corporate wellness programs) is named but never analyzed beyond generic re-identification boilerplate.
actionability_justification: The final report does name concrete techniques (k-anonymity, l-diversity, differential privacy, DPAs with misuse penalties, TLS, encrypted storage), but most guidance stays directional ('provide a clear privacy policy', 'establish data governance policies') and the specifics are buried in heavy repetition.
salient_examples: Reflection Questions 8-37 repeat the identical anonymization/DPA/transparency/security/governance block across six ASSISTANT turns
Use k-anonymity, l-diversity, or differential privacy techniques to protect user privacy (concrete, but repeated unchanged each turn)
Use data processing agreements (DPAs) ... include restrictions on data use and penalties for misuse
the report omits the core secondary-use/lawful-basis problem of selling mood data to employers, listing it only under 'not covered'
